# claude-bughunter

> A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **85 skills** · 16 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com).

Built by **Sachin Sharma** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

 
   SPONSORED BY 
   
   
   
     
       
       
     
   
        
   
     
       
       
     
   
 

---

## What is this?

`claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the Claude Code skills system. Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope.

Four layers stack:

- **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline.
- **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates.
- **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation.
- **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables.

All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name.

---

## Quickstart

**Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code:

```text
/plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
/plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls
```

All 85 skills + 16 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`.

**A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them.

git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git
cd Claude-BugHunter
```

# macOS / Linux
bash scripts/install.sh

# Windows (PowerShell)
pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1
```

Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## How it works

It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 

Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. 

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. 

Next up, once you say "go", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.

There's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Your coding agent just has Superpowers.

   "大道至简" 
 

 

中文 | English

 

* 此开源项目旨在完全从 0 开始，仅用 3 块钱成本与 2 小时训练时间，即可训练出规模约为 64M 的超小语言模型 MiniMind。
* MiniMind 系列极其轻量，主线最小版本体积约为 GPT-3 的 $\frac{1}{2700}$，力求让普通个人 GPU 也能快速完成训练与复现。
* 项目同时开源了大模型的极简结构与完整训练链路，覆盖 MoE、数据清洗、预训练（Pretrain）、监督微调（SFT）、LoRA、RLHF（DPO）、RLAIF（PPO / GRPO / CISPO）、Tool Use、Agentic RL、自适应思考与模型蒸馏等全过程代码。
* MiniMind 同时拓展了视觉模态模型 MiniMind-V、多模态 Omni 模型 MiniMind-O、扩散语言模型（MiniMind-dLM）、线性模型（MiniMind-Linear），详见 Discussion。
* 项目所有核心算法代码均从 0 使用 PyTorch 原生实现，不依赖第三方库提供的高层抽象接口。
* 这不仅是一个大语言模型全阶段开源复现项目，也是一套面向 LLM 入门与实践的教程。
* 希望此项目能为更多人提供一个可复现、可理解、可扩展的起点，一起感受创造的乐趣，并推动更广泛 AI 社区的进步。

> 注：本项目基于 Apache 2.0 协议开源，完全免费。“2 小时” 指 SFT 阶段在单张 NVIDIA 3090 上跑完 `1 epoch` 的实测耗时，“3 块钱” 指对应时段的 GPU 租用成本。

# 📌 项目介绍

大语言模型（Large Language Model, LLM）的出现，引发了全球范围内对 AI 的空前关注。无论是 ChatGPT、DeepSeek 还是 Qwen，都以惊艳的效果让人真切感受到这场技术浪潮的冲击力。然而，动辄数百亿参数的模型规模，使得它们对个人设备而言不仅难以训练，甚至连部署都显得遥不可及。打开大模型的“黑盒子”，真正去理解其内部运作机制，本应是一件令人心潮澎湃的事。遗憾的是，绝大多数探索最终都止步于使用 LoRA 等技术对现有大模型做少量微调，学习一些新指令或特定任务。这更像是在教牛顿如何使用 21 世纪的智能手机——虽然有趣，却偏离了理解物理本质的初衷。

与此同时，第三方的大模型框架与工具库，如 `transformers` / `trl` / `peft` 等，往往只暴露出高度抽象的接口。只需短短十几行代码，就可以完成“加载模型 + 加载数据集 + 推理 + 强化学习”的全流程训练。这种高效封装固然便利，却也在一定程度上把开发者与底层实现隔离开来，削弱了深入理解 LLM 核心代码的机会。我认为 “用乐高自己拼出一架飞机，远比坐在头等舱里飞行更让人兴奋”，然而更现实的问题是，互联网上充斥着大量付费课程和营销内容，用漏洞百出、一知半解的讲解包装所谓的 AI 教程。正因如此，本项目的初衷就是尽可能降低 LLM 的学习门槛，让每个人都能从理解每一行代码开始，从 0 开始亲手训练一个极小的语言模型。是的，从**零开始训练**，而不是仅仅停留在**推理**层面。最低只需不到 3 块钱的服务器成本，就能亲身体验从 0 到 1 构建一个语言模型的全过程。

😊 一起感受创造的乐趣吧！

- 提供 Tokenizer 与分词器训练代码，支持 ` `、` `、` ` 等模板标记。

- 提供全阶段开源数据，覆盖收集、蒸馏、清洗与去重后的高质量数据集。
- 关键训练算法与核心模块均从 0 实现，不依赖第三方框架封装。
- 兼容 `transformers`、`trl`、`peft` 等主流框架，以及 `llama.cpp`、`vllm`、`ollama` 等常用推理引擎与 `Llama-Factory` 等训练框架。
- 支持单机单卡与单机多卡（DDP、DeepSpeed）训练，支持 wandb / swanlab 可视化与动态启停训练。
- 支持在 C-Eval、C-MMLU、OpenBookQA 等第三方测评集上进行评测，并支持通过 YaRN 实现 RoPE 长文本外推。

# **🔥 Firecrawl**

**Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥** You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three.

- **Firecrawl Local.** Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost.
- **Firecrawl Cloud.** Use the hosted service at firecrawl.dev for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria for far more knowledge than scraping alone.
- **Self-hosting.** Deploy the full Firecrawl server from `apps/api` with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure.

_Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :)_

 
   
 

---

## Firecrawl Local

Firecrawl Local scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means `xcode-select --install` and on Debian or Ubuntu means `build-essential`.

```bash
cargo install firecrawl-local
```

If you don't have Rust, Firecrawl Cloud runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup.

```bash
npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev
```

Scrape a page and print its markdown.

```bash
firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown
```

Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page.

```bash
firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages
```

List every URL on a site.

```bash
firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev
```

Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning.

### Add it to your AI agent

`init` finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server. It backs up every config file first, and the MCP server itself needs Node.js 22 or newer.

```bash
firecrawl-local init
```

Restart your AI tool afterwards. Its scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape tools run on your machine, and the other Firecrawl tools go to Firecrawl Cloud.

### Run the Firecrawl API on localhost

`serve` answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key.

```bash
firecrawl-local serve
```

NGINX (pronounced "engine x" or "en-jin-eks") is the world's most popular Web Server, high performance Load Balancer, Reverse Proxy, API Gateway and Content Cache.

NGINX is free and open source software, distributed under the terms of a simplified 2-clause BSD-like license.

Enterprise distributions, commercial support and training are available from F5, Inc.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The goal of this README is to provide a basic, structured introduction to NGINX for novice users. Please refer to the full NGINX documentation for detailed information on installing, building, configuring, debugging, and more. These documentation pages also contain a more detailed Beginners Guide, How-Tos, Development guide, and a complete module and directive reference.

NGINX is installed software with binary packages available for all major operating systems and Linux distributions. See Tested OS and Platforms for a full list of compatible systems.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> While nearly all popular Linux-based operating systems are distributed with a community version of nginx, we highly advise installation and usage of official packages or sources from this repository. Doing so ensures that you're using the most recent release or source code, including the latest feature-set, fixes and security patches.

## Modules
NGINX is comprised of individual modules, each extending core functionality by providing additional, configurable features. See "Modules reference" at the bottom of nginx documentation for a complete list of official modules.

NGINX modules can be built and distributed as static or dynamic modules. Static modules are defined at build-time, compiled, and distributed in the resulting binaries. See Dynamic Modules for more information on how they work, as well as, how to obtain, install, and configure them.

```bash
nginx -V

items.content:
Open-source software toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models.
 

 
   Documentation   •   Blog   •   Key Features   •   Tutorials   •   Integrations   •   Benchmarks   •   Generative AI  
 

[](https://badge.fury.io/py/openvino)

[](https://pepy.tech/project/openvino)
[](https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/openvino/files)
[](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openvino)
  

- **Inference Optimization**: Boost deep learning performance in computer vision, automatic speech recognition, generative AI, natural language processing with large and small language models, and many other common tasks.
- **Flexible Model Support**: Use models trained with popular frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Keras, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax. Directly integrate models built with transformers and diffusers from the Hugging Face Hub using Optimum Intel. Convert and deploy models without original frameworks.
- **Broad Platform Compatibility**: Reduce resource demands and efficiently deploy on a range of platforms from edge to cloud. OpenVINO™ supports inference on CPU (x86, ARM), GPU (Intel integrated & discrete GPU) and AI accelerators (Intel NPU).
- **Community and Ecosystem**: Join an active community contributing to the enhancement of deep learning performance across various domains.

Check out the OpenVINO Cheat Sheet and Key Features for a quick reference.

## Installation

Get your preferred distribution of OpenVINO or use this command for quick installation:

```sh
pip install -U openvino
```

### Verify Installation

After installation, you can verify OpenVINO is installed correctly by running:

```python
import openvino as ov
print(ov.__version__)
```

Check system requirements and supported devices for detailed information.

## Tutorials and Examples

OpenVINO Quickstart example will walk you through the basics of deploying your first model.

Learn how to optimize and deploy popular models with the OpenVINO Notebooks 📚:
- Create an LLM-powered Chatbot using OpenVINO
- YOLOv11 Optimization
- Text-to-Image Generation
- Multimodal assistant with LLaVa and OpenVINO
- Automatic speech recognition using Whisper and OpenVINO

Discover more examples in the OpenVINO Samples (Python & C++) and Notebooks (Python).

Here are easy-to-follow code examples demonstrating how to run PyTorch and TensorFlow model inference using OpenVINO:

**PyTorch Model**

```python
import openvino as ov
import torch
import torchvision

# load PyTorch model into memory
model = torch.hub.load("pytorch/vision", "shufflenet_v2_x1_0", weights="DEFAULT")

# convert the model into OpenVINO model
example = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)
ov_model = ov.convert_model(model, example_input=(example,))

# compile the model for CPU device
core = ov.Core()
compiled_model = core.compile_model(ov_model, 'CPU')

# infer the model on random data

items.title: [推广] [发码] 做了个 AI 阅读器 ，我们想将 AI 和阅读器做深度结合，而不仅仅是简单问答
items.summary:
下面是我们已经做的 AI 功能，采用 BYOK 形式。

1. 阅读问答

读到不理解的词句，可以选中文字向 AI 提问。围绕原书内容随读随问，解释疑惑，帮助你理解正在阅读的内容。

2. 主动陪读

根据每本书的介入设置，在合适的时候提供续读回顾。当新读到的内容能够补充之前的问题时，也会适时给出跟进建议，帮助你衔接阅读思路。

3. 自动批注重点

阅读页面稳定后，AI 会复核少量关键原文，自动添加批注，并通过落笔动画呈现，帮助你抓住阅读重点。

4. 按策略标注

按照当前书籍的标注策略，自动标注当前可见原文中明确符合条件的内容，让阅读标记更贴合你的关注方向。

5. 双语阅读与翻译

生成并复核译文，辅助双语阅读，还可以提前翻译下一章，方便你在阅读原文时理解内容。

6. 导读与章节总结

生成导读、章节总结与相关学习内容，帮助你了解内容脉络、梳理章节重点，让阅读更有方向。

7. 书籍分析

分析书籍内容，推荐适合的阅读方式和辅助功能，帮助你判断这本书该怎么读、可以搭配哪些阅读工具。

8. 理解自检与练习

根据阅读内容生成自检问题与练习，检查理解情况，并提供批改反馈，帮助你发现尚未掌握的地方。

9. 书库助手

帮你查找书籍，并针对书库文件夹提出整理方案，让查书和整理书库更有条理。

10. 统一记录整理

检索并归纳已经保存的记录，整理阅读笔记，方便你回顾读过的内容与留下的想法。

11. 智能设置

通过文字或语音调整相关设置，也能解释 AI 用量，并打开需要你手动操作的配置卡片，让设置调整更方便。

12. 昨日总结

根据昨天实际阅读的内容与已保存的记录，生成阅读回顾，帮助你重新梳理昨日的重点与收获。

13. 今日发现

每天精选一篇与你阅读内容相关的外部文章，为阅读补充新的视角，发现值得继续了解的内容。

14. 自动长期记忆

从互动与阅读中自动提炼少量偏好，让后续提供的帮助更贴合你的阅读习惯与需求。

15. 扫描页面识别

使用支持视觉的 AI 模型识别扫描页面内容，为扫描版书籍的阅读提供辅助。

16. 智能朗读编排

提前判断人物与表达方式，配合调度可用声音，让朗读更贴合内容；播报过程不必等待 AI。

注：自动批注重点、按策略标注、智能朗读编排默认关闭，可按需开启。

25 年的 B300 比 24 年的 B200 算力高 1.6 倍
26 年的 R100 比 25 年的旗舰 算力高 3 倍  比三年前的 H200 理论算力要高 18～25 倍了

那再过两年，花大价钱部署的 H200 B200 直接淘汰的级别，卖二手都不一定有人接，卖出去可能也是骨折骨灰价格

或者说过两三年，这些卡会掉价进入普通用户市场

到时候不追求最新模型的普通用户，就能本地跑当前版本模型的无限 token

大家怎么看，预计无限 token 要多久进入家家户户
items.content: 按照 NVIDIA 的迭代速度，是不是现在投入买算力越狠的，后面淘汰的越快 - V2EX Home Sign Up Sign In V2EX › 问与答 按照 NVIDIA 的迭代速度，是不是现在投入买算力越狠的，后面淘汰的越快 break · 7h 41m ago · 1899 views 24 年的 B200 比 23 年的 H200 算力高两倍 25 年的 B300 比 24 年的 B200 算力高 1.6 倍 26 年的 R100 比 25 年的旗舰 算力高 3 倍 比三年前的 H200 理论算力要高 18～25 倍了 那再过两年，花大价钱部署的 H200 B200 直接淘汰的级别，卖二手都不一定有人接，卖出去可能也是骨折骨灰价格 或者说过两三年，这些卡会掉价进入普通用户市场 到时候不追求最新模型的普通用户，就能本地跑当前版本模型的无限 token 大家怎么看，预计无限 token 要多久进入家家户户 算力 淘汰 无限 24 replies • 2026-11-28 16:17:25 +08:00 break OP 7h 36m ago 1 后面是不是 NVIDIA 越赚钱，迭代越快，其他人死的越快 znedyrk 7h 12m ago 2 r100 比起 h200 要高这么多吗 怪不得不要了 nevin47 7h 2m ago 3 即便是 6 年前上市的，算力是 H200 1/3 的 A100（如果加上稀疏特性，A100 的实际算力可能比不过 H200 的 1/10） 云上 GPU 的价格大概 8 卡一个月也能租大几万出去，单卡二手差不多 5-8 万左右 所以现在担心两三年后 H200 淘汰，有点想的太远了。除非说未来出现什么模型，能力能达到当前 opus5 的水平，然后只有 100-200B 的参数量，那才会出现无限 token 走进千家万户 bgm004 6h 46m ago 4 无限 token？？？ 你当这些卡白菜价啊。这么多人买个云服务器都扣扣索索。手机套餐都嫌弃贵，就敢想无限 token 了。除非有便宜效果好的卡。 flyws 6h 32m ago 5 @ nevin47 非常同意。实际上生产中在很多缺卡的地区，T4 都还有人在大规模使用，查了一下这已经是 2018 年的卡了，现在仍然没有到想要用多少就能有多少的地步。 另外 B200 HGX 数据中心版本是 1000W，这不太是普通用户家里能放的，普通人家里可能最多能放个 RTX PRO 产品线。其实现在如果不是一个非常急性子的人，很多 AI 盒子或者 mac studio 这些已经足够让你满血 qwen3.8 27b 自由了，如果习惯多个 agent 同时上而且必须要快的话，我猜现在这么缺 GPU，我个人估计还得三到五年才能迭代出一个 decode 足够快的硬件 + 一个 coding 性能没什么大缺点的小模型（qwen 已经足够好，但就是原版 thinking 废话太多了） journalistFromHK 6h 4m ago 6 现在舍不得投入的后面应该也没机会买更先进的吧? apuslilie 5h 52m ago 7 行业高速增长的时候这都不是事儿，二手乃至 n 手的硬件都有自己的生态。 hafuhafu 5h 45m ago 8 算力只是不如新的，又不是归零了，为啥搞得和无价值破烂一样恨不得马上脱手... 该用一样用，又没啥影响。 而且只说用途的话，要用卡的地方太多了，就算不用来做 LLM 相关的训练或推理，传统音视频处理、非 LLM 推理之类的一样大把场景能用。 break OP 5h 13m ago 9 @ hafuhafu “高盛 2026 年的研究指出，AI 加速芯片通常按约 4—6 年的使用寿命估计，但经济性淘汰可能早于物理损坏。“ “路透社 2026 年 10 月 1 日的报道显示，部分贷款机构对 GPU 资产采取更加保守的 3—4 年折旧或估值假设” 旧卡会有剩余价值，但是价值没有想象的大，一个是物理使用寿命出厂设计就不是很久，一个是新的产品的竞争力差距。再过两年当时的 H100 物理寿命就快到期了。而且如果入手后，前三年没有回本，后续应该很难靠现成的卡回本了，因为价值曲线应该是下滑的 break OP 5h 11m ago 10 @ bgm004 流量套餐和这个完全不是一回事，流量必须有基站，这个普通人是不可能架设的，但是 token 有卡就有机会自己架设 ninjaJ 5h 7m ago 11 对公司来说，财务上的折旧到了就表示这张卡已经没有价值了，不管它物理上有没有坏或者怎样。不存在亏不亏的说法。 break OP 4h 55m ago 12 @ ninjaJ 你这个没太看懂，公司花 1000 万买卡，3 年后报废，靠卡赚取的利润是 700 万，这种情况不算亏吗？ ntdll 4h 52m ago 13 预计无限 token 要多久进入家家户户 可能性极低，几乎得是梦里才有可能。这违背了厂家商业利益。现在因为硬件成本高企，所以大模型厂家会开放模型权重，赚个名声，因为你根本也部署不了，玩家只能部署流口水的量化版本，能部署全精度版本的也不是小玩家。即使未来某一天，硬件成本足够低的时候，大模型厂家就不会开放权重给你自部署了。不然他们赚谁的钱去呢。 break OP 4h 40m ago 14 @ nevin47 @ flyws 当时是会要等的，毕竟现在头部企业们都缺算力，期待普通人接入无限 token 的时代，那个时候才能百花齐放 现在的自费上班 vibe coding，论坛已经是层出不穷的产品，到了普通人 token 无限，更多的创意才能爆发出来，有可能会是奇葩乱放，但是感觉会更热闹与精彩 以前是“就缺一个程序员”，现在是“尿性的 5 小时限额”“Misanthropic 的 A 畜”，现在时代的感觉就是大家都能感应到有一个瓶颈阻碍着自己的突破，但那个瓶颈有似乎不是牢不可破的，瓶颈之后的境界也隐约可见的感觉，只是“灵石”有限，灵气积累不够，还不足以一举突破 nevin47 4h 39m ago 15 @ break 他这个是按 IDC 独占去评估的，你去看 GCP AWS 上的租赁就知道他这个估计和实际市场脱节有多严重了 nevin47 4h 37m ago 16 @ break 要等模型到位才可能 strobber16 3h 53m ago via Android 17 不如买 amd lang1pal 3h 52m ago 18 折旧费很厉害，所以高溢价的芯片导致了算力成本远高于别人。我觉得如果不给蒸馏的话，ai 根本没法搞。 volvo007 3h 46m ago via iPhone 19 我部署了本地的 deepseek4.1 flash，4 dgx spark 非常好用，但和顶级闭源模型还是有差距。另外 4 卡 A100 上部署了 w4a16 的 qwen 3.8 flash next，16 路解码速度破千，后面给我这边小团队用 volvo007 3h 46m ago via iPhone 20 做梦都想搞个 dgx B300，售价 70w，国内要翻倍…… danhahaha

items.title: 有了 AI 之后，开发越来越容易，推广却越来越难？
items.summary:
最近用 AI 辅助开发了几个项目，感觉开发效率确实提高了不少，但产品上线后，怎么找到用户依然是个难题。

尤其是微信小程序，个人开发者似乎没有太多低成本的推广渠道。

于是最近又折腾了一个微信小程序版的 Product Hunt：https://minihunt.top

目前收录了 2000 多个小程序，支持开发者免费提交自己的作品，算是对产品推广方向的一次尝试。

想和大家讨论一下，当 AI 逐渐降低软件开发门槛之后，获取用户会不会成为独立开发者最大的挑战？

大家平时除了写代码，有没有研究过产品推广和获客？

items.summary:
我平时做视频，经常要把一条视频换成另一种语言：要么把中文视频发到海外，要么把生肉英文教程转成中文看。只翻字幕准确率堪忧，云端 AI 配音按分钟收费、声音还是那几个熟悉的「傲娇大姐孤独小帅」，自己手搓「扒词 → 翻译 → TTS → 对轨 → 压字幕」一条 5 分钟的片子能耗掉一下午。

所以我用原生 Swift 写了个 macOS 应用：**译哥 Poly**。视频拖进去点开始，不到 1 分钟出成片：换了语言、保留原片音色，双语字幕一并压好（目前中 ↔ 英）。

效果（47 秒中文口播 → 英文配音成片），官网首页能直接看视频：https://poly.uulili.com

![左边原片，右边译哥配好的英文版](https://poly.uulili.com/media/hero-poster.jpg)

### 适合场景和人群
* 单人口播：适合你把中文视频一键做成海外版发布（反过来也行）
* 软件录屏教程：让油管的高质量英文博主，开口说中文
* 课程讲座翻译：产品教程可以用这种方式翻译成其他语言
* 快速做双语字幕：为视频快速制作自己指定样式的双语字幕

### 核心功能和技术栈

![主界面：拖进去，点开始](https://poly.uulili.com/img/main.jpg)
识别和配音全部在 Apple Silicon 本机跑，视频不上传。

- **识别**：SenseVoice（sherpa-onnx）+ Silero VAD；英文、日文用系统语音识别。
- **翻译**：整句翻译，不按碎词断句。Apple Translation（免费、本机）/ Google / DeepSeek / 智谱等多种渠道，Key 安全存入钥匙串。走云端大模型时只发字幕文本，token 用量很低。
- **校对**：可选的校对窗口（设置里决定要不要介入），原文、配音字幕、断行都能改；支持大模型一键润色；还有术语表，自定义处理人名、品牌名这类逢听必错的词。
- **配音**：常规配音，或零样本克隆原片音色。内置 Qwen3-TTS 0.6B / 1.7B，`mlx-audio-swift` 跑在本机。不用录样本，自动从原片挑约 10 秒干净人声当参考。
- **对齐**：配音保持自然语速，反过来只让说话那几段的画面变速（最多 1.5 倍），原片的气口和停顿原样保留。
- **合成导出**：纯 AVFoundation，不依赖 ffmpeg，导出快到来不及看进度条。

当然里面还有很多细节，有快速断行、修改后自动翻译、字幕样式等等，主要是用户体验的优化，尽量确保用户在不用学习的情况下就知道怎么使用。

![字幕样式可以自己调](https://poly.uulili.com/img/style.jpg)

### 关键数据
- 硬件门槛：**Apple 芯片 Mac，macOS 26 及以上，8 GB 内存起**；
- 47 秒口播，M5 Pro 全流程 39 秒；38 秒样片，M2 Max 约 31 秒；
- 配音阶段内存峰值约 7 GB，8 GB 的 M1 MacBook Air 实测能跑完。

### 价格和送码
- 纯字幕功能永久免费；配音每个视频前 3 分钟免费导出（带水印）；
- 买断版首发 **¥69**，之后 ¥129。一次买断，没有订阅。解锁不限时长配音、去水印、1.7B 高质量配音模型、批量排队。

其实就相当于你请我吃顿便饭，我用 Poly 把你以后双语配音和字幕的事都包了。

**回帖送码**：回帖聊聊你最想拿它翻什么视频，或者直接拍砖提建议呦。12 月 4 日 前我从回复里挑 10 位送买断版激活码。

官网：https://poly.uulili.com

items.title: 用闪极充电头充电导致 MacBook Pro 损坏
items.summary:
有一段时间持续用闪极充电头给 M 芯片的 MacBook Pro 充电，有一天电脑突然黑屏断电，然后再也无法开机，用原装磁吸充电也没反应了。天才吧说主板已无任何响应，需要更换主板，最后找第三方把主板上的电源芯片换了就好了。再也不敢用第三方的充电头了，用了很久都没问题，但是一出问题就是大问题。

items.content: Commitment issues (app edition) - by Ben Tossell Ben’s Bites Subscribe Sign in Commitment issues (app edition) It’s not me, it’s you Ben Tossell Nov 24, 2026 54 1 1 Share Last week, a mathematician spent six weeks with Claude and proved the Riemann hypothesis. A maths problem nobody had cracked since 1859. Then there’s me. I built a clock. P.s. The full interactive version of this post is here . Something in my tiny pea brain stops me working out What time is 10am PT in UK? without using super intelligence. I’m not proud of my chat history. It’s as bad as my calculator history. 200+65 is 265 btw. My clock lives in my menu bar. Type a time and a city, or drag it, and every city changes. presets for demo only It handles daylight savings too. Because of course the UK and US change their clocks on different weekends. You may be thinking ‘There’s a million clock apps that do this for free’. And you’re absolutely right. But I’ve got commitment issues. I’m always window shopping. Lots of apps are good enough but it feels like the grass is always greener. A lot of great tools come down to a few small features I really like. But they’re not making it for me. They’re making it for everyone. They need more users, so they add more features, and they put the price up. Or they’re free and get forgotten. It’s not me, it’s you. And I’m no better with AI models. Right now I’m using Gemini 4 Neon after turning my back on Google. A new model comes around and I pack my bags and move in. I obviously need the best to answer my very hard questions. The trouble with juggling multiple models at once is keeping track of them. Who am I neglecting? Who’s about to cut me off? Other apps I tried had more than I needed, so I made a stripped down version with just the things I care about. sliding usage is just used to show the menu icon syncing Screenshots are another one. I take a lot of full-page screenshots. Things I’ve built, to check them, or sites I like the look of, to ‘borrow’ from. So now I have an extension that does that. Browsers are a different beast. They’re a marriage. We spend a lot of time in them. So this relationship has been one of my biggest headaches. I’m sure I could build my own but it feels like a lot of work. I loved Arc, like many others. Then they got bought and ditched it. So I went back to Chrome. Then the people behind Arc came out with Dia, so I went crawling back to my ex, who’d had some work done. It was kinda the same but not quite. Then I dated someone literally named after both of my exes, Arc and Dia - Ardia. No red flags there. Then it got slow. So I stopped looking and just taught Chrome all my ex’s best moves: A way to ‘peek’ links - which shows you a mini window of the page you click Click to open a page in split view Vertical tabs (Chrome added this anyway) Ad blocking, no cookie banners And my biggest need - the tab switcher. I built my own extension + mac app that does all of that. Plus I can add in some extra niceties like defaultin

Before we do the maths, people have been trying versions of this for 256 years. Nearly all of them shut down or got caught. None of them came close to today’s scale. So what would it actually take? Let’s be generous. Assume everyone types at world-record speed, 200 words a minute, non-stop. Everyone is happy to wait 10 minutes for a reply. And it’s a remote company spread across every time zone, so someone is always awake. The average ChatGPT user sends about 4 messages a day, and a reply is roughly 500 words now. With over a billion people using the big AI chatbots, that’s about 6 billion messages every day. 10.4 million people typing at world-record speed, round the clock, with no sleep, no lunch, and no days off. Okay, let’s run it like a real company instead. Which means it needs a CEO. Me. 11.8 billion internal messages a day, just to keep the place running. Oh, and we still have to answer the 6 billion messages people actually sent us. All in, you’d need 77.4 million staff just to keep 10.4 million people typing at any given moment. If you want to check my maths: a 40-hour week, time off from a 2025 survey of UK call centres , 12.1 people per manager ( the US average ), and 2 HR people per 100 staff ( SHRM ). People quit at the US rate , earn the US median for customer service , and get 153 chat messages a day , like the average Microsoft Teams user. The biggest Zoom call holds 1 million . He picked a line from a book, hid it from his wife Betty, and got her to guess it one letter at a time. Betty didn’t know the sentence, she just knew the patterns of English. My wife does this to me every day. She’s had years of practice. So what if we replaced Betty with a computer? For more than 60 years, the answer was no. Giving machines more to read barely helped, because they could only see the last couple of words. Try guessing what comes after “speak fluent…” with no other clues. In 2017, eight people at Google let it see every word at once and weigh the ones that matter, like France. They called that attention, and the machine a transformer. It’s the T in ChatGPT. Suddenly, giving it more to read actually worked. More text, bigger brain, better guesses. Writing a reply is the same thing. items.content: Productiv-icky - by Ben Tossell - Ben's Bites Ben’s Bites Subscribe Sign in Productiv-icky Digging holes on the beach Ben Tossell Nov 17, 2026 79 4 2 Share productiv-icky (adj.) - the feeling of doing work you didn’t mean to do We have a problem. full interactive post is here We agree this is insane, right? Someone I don’t know sends me emails that I’m expected to reply to. I don’t know them. I don’t work for them. So I ignore them (well actually I send them to email jail). Nuh-uh, that’s not my work, buddy. But it’s different if it’s my super-intelligent, helpful agent friend… Yeses are easy. They’re quick. But every yes has a yes-tax. The hidden extra work you didn’t think of. The long tail of regret where you question why you ever said yes. Say I did reply to those emails, they’d send me stuff to read to show how great they are at their job and how much better I’d be. Then we’d organise a call (which would derail whichever day that call was on). Then we’d have follow-up items. Then a string of other crap I couldn’t care less about. I know what’s going to happen. I can smell it, it stinks. I’ve said yes and paid the tax many times before. Now I pay $200/mo for a super-intelligent, over-eager, needy little nerd to ping me incessantly about taking things off my plate. I feel bad for him. He wants to work. He’s gagging for it. Just. One. More. Task. Master. Plus, my little nerd has a gambling problem. Or rather, he feeds mine. Remember years ago sending tons of Slack messages to get the most out of your $20/mo plan? Nor me. Why? Because it’s dumb. But now we feel like we should use all our tokens before they run out. Why? Because everyone else is. We started measuring shovels instead of the hole. Someone’s needy little nerd booked their dentist, replied to their mum and launched a business whilst they were asleep. They’ve got an org chart. For nerds. With a Chief of Staff. You feel behind. Like way behind. So you grab a shovel and start digging. A little hole over there to triage your inbox, one here to draft your tweets, one to check on those. Then you spend your day checking the holes are being dug right. Before long, you’re surrounded by holes and a mountain of dirt you gotta do something with. Now as a man, holes are hardwired into my DNA. A few beers, a beach and a shovel, I’m digging a hole. I’d take pride in it. I’d make the best one, impressively round, deep enough to see sea water seep through the bottom. But I’d only dig one. There’s a whole beach but I chose this spot. Next time the needy little nerd pings you: do you really want another hole? Also, don’t dig big holes on the beach. They collapse. If you haven’t read it, you can get a copy here . I have had the chance to use the new Claude Fable 5.2 quite a bit before its public launch 1 , and it is very impressive, following on the already excellent Opus 5.5. AI has gotten so good, in fact, that it is worth asking if Anthropic’s newest models (and the inevitable competing models OpenAI and Google will soon release) cross the boundary into being an Artificial General Intelligence? AGI is a much-debated term with a lot of potential definitions. For this post, I’ll go with: “an AI as good as most human experts at most intellectual tasks you can do with a computer.” This explicitly excludes a lot of human work, including interacting with the physical world and other people, as well as most actual jobs, where “using a computer” is just one task among many. Still, even with these caveats, building a limited form of AGI has long been the goal of AI developers. So as not to keep you in suspense, I think the answer is that this is “almost” AGI, or what I have called Jagged AGI. Even within my limited definition, there are still important areas in many tasks where AI is jagged enough to fall well behind human capability. But the jaggedness is no longer about simple errors or hallucinations, which makes it harder to describe. So I want to try to do that in this post by showing you what Fable can do and where the gaps are. To get started I asked the new model: “I write OneUsefulThing among other stuff, I need you to create the most impressive thing I can share with people when you launch. It needs to be embeddable in a post and i can preface it however you like. it needs to have a visceral impact on people to show what you can do and the range of capabilities. It should grab them quickly. Be amazingly clever about this.” Fable asked me not to reveal anything until you had watched its video to the end. This was in one shot, with no feedback from me beyond the prompt. There is creativity here (including in the twist ending) and judgment and playfulness and cleverness. items.content: 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts) - by Ethan Mollick One Useful Thing Subscribe Sign in 30 Months on the Exponential (in Charts) My new book is out today... what happened since the last one Ethan Mollick Oct 20, 2026 826 150 71 Share My second book on AI, Co-Existence, is out today (and you can get it here ), 30 months after the release of Co-Intelligence in early 2024. Looking back across the gap between these books is a good way to get a sense of AI progress. And, thanks to AI, I can describe this progress with some quite lovely charts. Making the charts is itself a good indicator of how far things have come. In the era of chatbots, the era of Co-Intelligence , I would have had to work back-and-forth with an AI in a chat window, guiding it through each new step. In the current era of agentic AI that I cover in Co-Existence , I delegated the work and let the AI handle it. In this case, I used Opus 5.5 in Claude Projects, which allows you to talk to a single “orchestrator” agent that then spins off additional agents as needed, giving them instructions and relaying information back to you. Getting the work done was straightforward. I gave the AI a couple sentences of suggestions and it did what would have taken me hours of work (all the research, all the graphing, all the layouts, all the images, all the citations…) in minutes. And since I didn’t have to do the work, I had the AI make many options for me. I picked some and gave handwavy reactions to others that would drive a human team mad (“make it better”). It even caught that I’d gotten the math wrong. I was going to call this post “28 months on the exponential.” Some examples of interacting with Claude to make the graphics for this post. Notice that it corrected me. “This is the worst AI you will ever use” I wrote this in my last book on AI, and it has continued to be literally true at every moment since. From early 2023 through early 2024, there was a single AI model that was undeniably the best in the world: GPT-4 from OpenAI. This was the AI model that most people remember from the first couple years of AI use, it was the one I thought about while writing Co-Intelligence , and it was the one that gave ChatGPT its status as the default AI for many people. Since then, twenty different AI models have held the lead at one time or another, all from Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI. Which company had the best AI model in the world. But the changing lead alone hides an even bigger change. In the last year I have been posting about how I suspected that humans would have to approach working with agents as a manager, deciding how to delegate work to agents and specifying how those agents should be organized. I thought that getting agents to work effectively as a group would take careful construction, akin to building a company, and that this would take time to figure out. Nope. I fell prey to The Bitter Lesson, the hard truth, learned over and over again, that things that we thought required elaborate human rules and thinking can be solved with the brute force of better machine learning systems and more AI. The Bitter Lesson is everywhere among AI startups and companies adopting AI. A huge amount of effort went into building elaborate computer systems to feed AIs the right information at the right time, but AI systems have learned to seek out information themselves. The same thing happened to prompting. People built elaborate templates and chains of prompts that walked the AI through a task one step at a time. Then newer models turned out to be better at planning the steps themselves, and, as our research shows , planning steps have much less value. The history of the Bitter Le— — you know what? I don’t really need to explain the Bitter Lesson, I asked Claude to do it in a music video. Nathan Lambert Nov 14, 2026 129 24 21 Share Article voiceover 0:00 -7:28 Audio playback is not supported on your browser. Please upgrade. The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a major setback for the US development of an open model ecosystem. Nvidia still has the financial interests in supporting open models, which are to avoid concentration in power among a few customers who would develop their own chips and reduce Nvidia’s profits, but supporting the open ecosystem is a tricky puzzle more than an engineering problem to grind out a solution on. Nvidia’s business operations are famously extremely dependent on Jensen as an operator, so it is a consensus opinion that there are challenges ahead (or even more high-profile departures through chip-smuggling investigations or plain-old sharks circling more poachable talent). Nvidia’s number one goal is to stabilize the ship, deliver to customers in the next 24 months, and prevent implosion. Open models have been one of Jensen’s more ambitious, founder-style bets. He has been flooding the zone with funding in a way that will very likely dry up. Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. Subscribe In this period, the open model economy is in its nascency. These are crucial years for establishing use-cases, revenue flow, and motives to continue training the next generation models. I discussed the sensitivity of these early years in my recent talk at Fireworks Forge ( slides , recording ). The core of the argument is one upside for open models, a reason to be optimistic, and one downside. The positive case is that the open model economy has correctly latched onto “ownership of intelligence” and enterprise post-training as a crucial lane. What is to be determined is exactly how big the downstream market is. The downside is that the true long-term benefit of open models, as truly commoditized intelligence, is very far from realization with compute in such short supply. In the near term, where inference startups are also struggling to get enough chips (because Anthropic and OpenAI are buying so much capacity), there’s little margin competition on open-weight models. If open-source models are also served at giant inference margins, as we learned with DeepSeek’s DeepInfer release, they’re far from a commodity. In this paradigm, the closed labs with better economies of scale and integration from model to datacenter and chips will win. I expanded on this challenge in my recent piece on the open model economy . Together, a lot still needs to go right for open models to be a meaningful economic engine. Nathan Lambert Nov 04, 2026 ∙ Paid 50 3 Share My longest running agent testbed has been building the Interconnects Dashboard — an aggregator of all of the best data on open model adoption and performance from across the web. This dashboard is freely available and becoming quite useful. Still, all the measurements we have on open model adoption are incredibly imprecise. We have noisy platform metrics, marketing-related metrics from startups, and imperfect public evaluations. It takes an informed eye to figure out where things are going. These research notes are my current best approximations of where we stand. As with most things on Interconnects, our goal is to build well more value than we capture, so the data on the dashboard will remain free for the foreseeable future. These notes will be more raw than many of my articles, a place for sharing what I’m mulling over but don’t have complete evidence for (yet). items.content: Was I wrong about open models & cyber risks? Subscribe Sign in Was I wrong about open models & cyber risks? Nathan Lambert Oct 30, 2026 70 21 10 Share Article voiceover 0:00 -9:46 Audio playback is not supported on your browser. Please upgrade. Last week coined the term “ Black October “ after an onslaught of critical vulnerability disclosures, including PHP2Shell and a long-standing GitLab bug, signified the moment when the cyber risks of AI models started to materialize. It seemed like the news cycle had stabilized a bit when I started writing this, but then there was news about another major crypto security incident at Binance . The crypto industry has a very long history of hacks , so it’s not the best industry to indicate vulnerabilities translating into new societal harm. Still, we are very much still living through the implications of this transition. The best guess for what is happening in the cybersecurity space is that the behind the scenes work has only accelerated, bringing more people and resources in to try and patch the internet — the Wall Street Journal reported that cyber first responders are strained , which seems like the system working. We’re living through this plot of an exponential rise in vulnerabilities, which will take a long time to level off at the top of the sigmoid. A few weeks ago, before the rapid acceleration in vulnerability disclosures and the uptick in reported hacks, I wrote the following take. It’s been getting a pretty consistent barrage of feedback, some hopeless dunk attempts and some reasonable discussion, so I wanted to unpack where I stand. Share Open-weight Mythos in April would’ve been fine? When Claude Mythos was announced, it was previewed as if it was a new class of cyber weapon, where if it ended up in the wrong hands it would’ve caused mass societal destabilization. It seems like this was wrong. By all measures, GLM-5.3 is the model that crosses that threshold of capability, and there’s little public evidence that much has changed, and we’re over a month out of the model weight release. In fact, I would go further. If Claude Mythos was accidentally released as open-weight, it seems like the world would have been more or less fine. Yes, there would be a clear increase in cybersecurity incidents and it would be bad for society if the model leaked, but it would be a scenario that looks more like an acceleration than a step change in risk.
